# Usage notes Mr Tanaka explains (languages/ja/notes.json). note-<id>-title and note-<id>.

note-desu-masu-title = です and ます
note-desu-masu = Polite sentences end in です (desu, "is") or a verb in its ます (masu) form: わかります, "I understand". Change ます to ません for "not": わかりません. To strangers, shopkeepers and your landlady, stay polite; the plain forms are for friends.

note-tsu-title = Counting with つ
note-tsu = For counting things, one to nine, Japanese has its own numbers ending in つ (tsu): 一つ hitotsu, 二つ futatsu, 三つ mittsu, 四つ yottsu, 五つ itsutsu. They work for almost anything: お茶を二つ, "two teas". Prices and money use the other numbers: 五百円, gohyaku en.

note-wa-ga-title = は and が
note-wa-ga = は (written "ha", said wa) marks what you're talking about: わたしは…です, "as for me, I'm …". が (ga) marks the thing itself, often something new or asked about: お金がありません, "there's no money". When in doubt, は for "as for", が before あります.

note-o-title = を
note-o = を (written "wo", said o) marks the thing an action is done to: お茶をください, "tea, please" (literally "please give tea"); ラーメンを食べます, "I eat ramen". It comes straight after the thing.
